title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Expansion Runway & Management Audit
book_title: Chapter 5: The Operator's Dashboard — Six KPIs & Management Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: Execution in specialty chemicals is measured by commissioning dates, utilization curves, and cash conversion—not investor-day slide decks.
epigraph.author: Capital Allocation Principle

web_blocks.html: Tanfac is shifting from a legacy acid maker into a multi-product fluorochemicals platform [1][4]. Headline quarterly sales alone can easily mislead during this shift [1][4]. To track the business fairly over the next eight quarters, we should watch six leading Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) [1][4][8][9]. These metrics track plant use, spread strength, raw-material risk, working capital, and capex delivery [1][4][8][9].

web_blocks.html: TAM & Expansion Runway: Tanfac's addressable market is growing along two clear tracks. First, India's domestic solar PV build-out needs ultra-pure DHF for TOPCon and HJT cell etching [4][8][12]. Management even sees scope to scale Solar DHF toward 20,000+ TPA over time [4][8][12]. Second, the global Kigali Amendment shifts cooling demand toward lower-GWP gases like HFC-32 (R-32), alongside fluorinated inputs for electronics and energy storage [4][8][12]. To fund its ₹495 crore, 20,000 MTPA downstream plant at Cuddalore, Tanfac boosted its equity in mid-2026 [4][8][9]. It raised a ₹250 crore Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) and a ~₹99.41 crore preferential issue [4][8][9]. Per ICRA, ~65% of the new plant's output is pre-sold, led by the 7-year, 7,500 MTPA Japanese deal worth ₹337.5 crore a year from January 2027 [4][8][9]. Management also aims to scale fluorinated chemicals, polymers, and HFOs across FY28–CY30 [4].

web_blocks.title: CEO & Management Walk-the-Talk Audit (FY2022–FY2026)
paragraphs: Disclosure Scope Note: Tanfac Industries does not host quarterly earnings conference calls, so this walk-the-talk audit relies on BSE filings, annual reports, and ICRA rating rationales [1][4][5].

Leadership Continuity & Transition: Long-serving Managing Director K. Sendhil Naathan passed away in April 2025 [4][8]. Tanfac named Afzal Malkani as Managing Director on January 9, 2026, working with CEO Hemango Gupta and Anupam Rasayan's technical team [4][8].

Promises Kept (Execution Credits): Management hit its main plant goals on time. It doubled AHF capacity to 29,700 MTPA on October 7, 2024 largely from internal cash [11]. It started Phase 1 (June 2025) and Phase 2 (October 2025) of India's first 10,000 TPA Solar-Grade DHF plant [3][12]. It signed the 7-year ₹2,362.5 crore Japanese supply deal [9] and pre-funded the R-32 build via QIP instead of heavy debt [4].

Watchpoints & Misses: Operating margins cooled faster than peak-cycle bulls hoped, dropping from 24% in FY25 to 16% in FY26 and 12% in Q2 FY27 [1]. The preferential issue size was trimmed down to ~₹99.41 crore from early plans [4]. Working capital also slipped as Days Payable shrank to 21 days, pulling CFO/EBITDA down to 56% [1].

web_blocks.html: Capital Deployment & Fundraising Mechanics (2026): Tanfac's mid-2026 fundraising shows careful pre-funding of its ₹495 crore, 20,000 MTPA downstream plant [4][8]. In June 2026, Tanfac closed a ₹250 crore Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) and a revised ~₹99.41 crore preferential share issue with promoter backing [4]. Together, those deals raised ~₹349.4 crore in fresh equity [4]. Paired with ₹136 crore of debt as of September 2026 and internal cash flow, this equity keeps Tanfac net debt-free on a post-QIP cash basis [1][4]. It also supports the ₹153 crore of CWIP already on the September 2026 books [1][4].

For management's FY2028–CY2030 roadmap—which aims beyond R-32 into fluorinated polymers, HFOs, and battery electrolytes—FY2027 is the key test [4][8]. Investors should watch three clear gates. First, does the 10,000 TPA Solar-Grade DHF plant stabilize above 70% utilization [1][9]? Second, does the 20,000 MTPA R-32 and fluorinated chemicals unit finish on time to start the ₹337.5 crore/year Japanese deal on January 1, 2027 [1][9]? Third, does blended OPM recover from Q2 FY2027's 12% low back toward management's 15%–18% baseline goal [1][9]?

web_blocks.html: Governance & Succession Resilience: Leadership changes in mid-cap chemical firms often stall plant builds, especially after an unexpected MD loss [4]. After K. Sendhil Naathan passed away in April 2025, Tanfac kept projects moving at Cuddalore [3][4][8]. It started Solar DHF Phases 1 and 2 in June and October 2025, then named Afzal Malkani as Managing Director in January 2026 alongside CEO Hemango Gupta [3][4][8]. That continuity, backed by Anupam Rasayan's technical bench, shows real team depth rather than one-person reliance [4]. Even so, analysts must watch working-capital recovery and R-32 start dates through FY2027. CWIP has already reached ₹153 crore, and any delay past January 2027 would push back sales against rising depreciation [1][9].

book_paragraphs: Once a chemical firm enters a heavy build phase, headline sales growth turns into a poor dashboard. Sales can rise just because a new kiln pushes out more tonnes at thin spreads. That is why we need an operator's dashboard: six leading KPIs that show if Tanfac's Cuddalore build is creating real value or just burning cash.

First is plant use at the doubled 29,700-tonne AHF unit started in October 2024. That line drove the jump from ₹557 crore in FY2025 to ₹711 crore in FY2026. Keeping those kilns full is vital to absorb higher depreciation. Second is the ramp-up of the 10,000-tonne Solar-Grade DHF plant started in June and October 2025. Because Solar DHF replaces imports for local TOPCon and HJT solar cell lines, its client uptake will show how fast Tanfac's mix shifts upmarket.

Third—and most urgent—is Operating Profit Margin. After peaking at 24% in FY2025, OPM fell to 16% in FY2026 and slid to 12% in the September 2026 quarter. Management guides for 15% to 18% EBITDA margins on base lines, with specialties lifting the blend over time. Watching if OPM steadies above 15% or drops below 12% will show if pricing power holds. Fourth is landed fluorspar cost and non-China share, since raw materials took ₹63.78 of every ₹100 in FY2026. Fifth is the Cash Conversion Cycle and CFO-to-EBITDA ratio, which weakened to 115 days and 56% in FY2026. Sixth is execution on the ₹495 crore, 20,000-tonne R-32 and fluorinated chemicals plant, where CWIP hit ₹153 crore by September 2026.

How does management score on a 3-to-5-year Walk-the-Talk audit? Because Tanfac Industries does not host quarterly earnings concalls, our audit relies strictly on BSE filings, annual reports, and ICRA rating rationales. Give credit where due. Despite a tough transition after Managing Director K. Sendhil Naathan passed away in April 2025, the team kept moving. Tanfac named Afzal Malkani as MD in January 2026 alongside CEO Hemango Gupta, and hit its main plant dates. They doubled AHF on time in October 2024 and launched India's first Solar DHF plant in 2025. They also signed a 7-year ₹2,362.5 crore Japanese deal starting January 2027. Better yet, they funded the ₹495 crore R-32 build mainly with ₹250 crore of QIP equity and a ₹99.41 crore preferential issue instead of heavy debt. Still, an honest audit notes the misses: the preferential issue was trimmed, working capital loosened, and margins fell fast from FY2025 peaks.

Look closely at the mid-2026 equity raise. Instead of borrowing ₹400 crore from banks to build the 20,000-tonne R-32 plant, management raised ₹250 crore via QIP and ₹99.41 crore via a preferential issue. That diluted existing shares by roughly 10%, lifting share capital from ₹10 crore to ₹11 crore and reserves from ₹363 crore to ₹726 crore. Yet in a cyclical chemical firm where margins just fell from 24% to 12%, pre-funding capex with equity instead of floating-rate debt is textbook risk control.

Over the next twelve months, three gates will decide if management's Walk-the-Talk grade stays positive. First, does Solar-Grade DHF scale smoothly across Indian TOPCon and HJT cell lines? Second, does the ₹495 crore downstream plant start cleanly enough to begin the ₹337.5 crore-a-year Japanese deal in January 2027? Third, does blended EBITDA margin recover from September 2026's 12% back into management's 15% to 18% band?

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Raising ₹250 crore via QIP and ₹99.41 crore via preferential shares before building a ₹495 crore R-32 plant shows cautious finance. This firm remembers carrying ₹69 crore of debt on ₹120 crore of sales back in FY2015. Equity dilution trims near-term ROE, yet prevents solvency stress if spreads stay soft.

book_subsections.title: The Japanese Contract as an Execution Anchor
paragraphs: In January 2026, Tanfac signed a 7-year deal to supply 7,500 tonnes a year of fluorinated chemicals to a Japanese buyer. Worth ₹337.5 crore a year and ₹2,362.5 crore in total starting January 2027, it pre-sells roughly 37.5% of the new 20,000-tonne plant before one drum ships. Now the job shifts to starting on time and passing Japanese quality audits with clean yields.
If Tanfac delivers on schedule, that single deal adds nearly half of FY2026's entire sales base in steady export revenue.

book_subsections.title: Solar PV & Kigali Tailwinds vs. Execution Reality
paragraphs: Both macro drivers—India's local solar cell build-out and the global Kigali shift toward R-32—bring real multi-year demand. Yet macro tailwinds never guarantee plant profits. Only high plant use and tight working capital turn market demand into free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Why QIP Discipline Protects Downside in Cyclical Chemistry
paragraphs: Many Indian chemical expansions fail not from bad chemistry, but because debt bills hit during a two-year margin trough. Keeping debt at ₹136 crore against ₹737 crore of net worth as of September 2026 shields Tanfac. Even a slow R-32 ramp-up will not cause balance-sheet distress.

book_subsections.title: Testing Leadership Continuity Under Stress
paragraphs: An unscripted test of team depth arrived in April 2025 when Managing Director K. Sendhil Naathan passed away. In many mid-sized industrial firms, losing a veteran MD mid-build stalls decisions for a year. At Tanfac, the team kept Cuddalore running, started both phases of Solar-Grade DHF on time in June and October 2025, and named Afzal Malkani as MD in January 2026 with CEO Hemango Gupta. They also closed the ₹2,362.5 crore Japanese deal and the ₹250 crore QIP in early 2026.

That steady execution earns real respect, yet does not grant a blank check. The same team must now restore Days Payable from 21 days toward past norms, lift CFO-to-EBITDA back above 70%, and start the ₹495 crore R-32 plant without cost overruns.
